slot.brief: Give the electronic configuration of a lanthanide/transition ion in its ground state; count unpaired electrons and compute the spin-only or effective magnetic moment.

stem: For gaseous $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ ($Z=24$), choose its ground-state configuration, number of unpaired electrons and spin-only moment. Use $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$.

verdicts.working: Cr is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹. Removing two electrons (4s first) gives Cr²⁺: [Ar] 3d⁴. In the gaseous ground state, the four d electrons are unpaired, so μ = √(4×6) = 4.90 BM.

working:
$\text{Cr}=[\text{Ar}]\,3d^5 4s^1$
$\text{Cr}^{2+}=[\text{Ar}]\,3d^4$ (remove $4s$ first)
$n=4$ (Hund's rule)
$\mu=\sqrt{4(4+2)}=\sqrt{24}=4.90\ \text{BM}$

Independent check: Cr is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹. Removing two electrons (4s first) gives Cr²⁺: [Ar] 3d⁴. In the gaseous ground state, the four d electrons are unpaired, so μ = √(4×6) = 4.90 BM.
solution: Neutral Cr is $[\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^5 4s^1$; removing the $4s$ electron first gives $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}=[\mathrm{Ar}]\,3d^4$. By Hund’s rule, $n=4$ unpaired electrons, so $$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{4(6)}=4.90\ \mathrm{BM}.$$
